newsitem.title: CUBA: Cuba asks for U.N. to help after Hurricane Lili.
newsitem.headline: Cuba asks for U.N. to help after Hurricane Lili.

text.p: Cuba asked the United Nations on Monday for humanitarian assistance to help recover from the effects of Hurricane Lili, which it called a "national tragedy."

Foreign Minister Roberto Robaina told representatives of U.N. agencies in Havana that Cuba urgently needed food, medicines, construction and agricultural material. The hurricane, which swept through central and western areas of Cuba on Thursday and Friday, caused extensive damage to crops such as bananas and citrus and flattened sugar cane fields.

There was also widespread damage to property. The national civil defence organisation said 5,640 homes were destroyed and about 84,000 suffered some sort of damage. Parts of the country were without power on Monday and one town in central Villa Clara province, Sagua la Grande, was still flooded.

Robaina said it was too early to give a precise estimate of the damage caused by Lili. But a statement handed to U.N. representatives said the storm had caused serious damage to eight of the country's 14 provinces, especially to food crops.

"The country is facing a real national tragedy which obliges us to postpone plans and dreams," Robaina said. He added the damage caused by Lili would inevitably have an impact on the pace of Cuba's economic recovery.

The communist-ruled island is struggling to emerge from five years of economic crisis caused by the collapse of its old economic ally the former Soviet bloc. Before Hurricane Lili, authorities had said the country was heading for Gross Domestic Product (GDP) growth of five percent this year.

Robaina said Cuba was directing its appeal to the specialised development agencies of the United Nations. But he said ambassadors from several foreign governments had already asked about the extent of the damage caused by Lili and about possible assistance Cuba might need.
"To them, we are simply explaining the situation and the world will decide how to react," Robaina said.
